findings.title: SendGrid client used for cancellation without an API key
findings.body: The new cancellation block calls `client.request({url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST", ...})` using the singleton exported by `@sendgrid/client`, but this module only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (line 19). `@sendgrid/mail` holds its own internal `Client` instance, so `setApiKey` on it does not configure the imported `client` singleton (compare `emailReminderManager.ts`, which explicitly calls `client.setApiKey(...)`). As a result every cancellation request here is sent unauthenticated and will fail with 401, the error is swallowed by the surrounding catch, and the "cancelled" reminders will still be delivered by SendGrid – i.e. the bug this PR is supposed to fix is not actually fixed in the CRON path. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this file.

findings.title: One failing cancellation aborts the whole cancellation batch and leaves DB rows untouched forever
findings.body: The whole `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop is wrapped in a single try/catch. If any single `client.request(...)` throws (invalid/expired batch id, SendGrid already has the batch in `cancel` status, transient 5xx), the loop is abandoned: all remaining reminders in the batch are never cancelled and their emails get sent. In addition, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` objects are Prisma lazy promises that only execute when awaited in `Promise.all` at line 74; because the throw happens before that await, none of the already-processed reminders are deleted. On the next CRON run the same reminders are selected again, the same request fails again, and the cancellation pass is permanently stuck. Each reminder needs its own try/catch (and its delete should be awaited/committed per item).

findings.title: remindersToCancel query is missing method/referenceId filters
findings.body: `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` does not filter on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` nor on `referenceId: { not: null }`, unlike every other query in this file. Any row that is flagged `cancelled` but has no `referenceId`, or that belongs to a non-email method, is posted to the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint with `batch_id: null`/a Twilio SID, which produces an error that (per the single try/catch above) aborts the whole cancellation pass. Restrict the query to email reminders with a non-null `referenceId`.

findings.title: immediateDelete path re-introduces the pending-cancellation accumulation and leaks reminder rows
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function issues the SendGrid `scheduled_sends` cancel immediately and returns without touching the `workflowReminder` row. Two problems: (1) the row stays in the DB with `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`, so it is neither deleted nor flagged – it lingers until the generic `deleteMany` in the CRON removes it after `scheduledDate` passes, and it can be "cancelled" again by later code paths; (2) this path is used for the two most common operations – rescheduling (`handleNewBooking.ts` line 968) and workflow/step deletion (`workflows.tsx` lines 214 and 521) – which means those cancellations still pile up as pending cancellations in SendGrid (the 100-pending limit described in the PR description) and will again start failing silently, so cancelled emails will still be delivered. These paths should use the same deferred `cancelled` flag mechanism as booking cancellation.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are no longer awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked fire-and-forget inside `forEach`. Previously the DB work for reminders was part of `prismaPromises` and therefore awaited before the handler returned. Now the handler can return (and in a serverless/edge deployment the invocation can be frozen or torn down) before the `workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` / Twilio cancel + row delete have completed, in which case the reminder is never marked cancelled and the workflow email/SMS is still sent – exactly the bug being fixed. Rejections are also unobserved (unhandled promise rejections). Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (line 488) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (line 966).

findings.title: try/catch around the reminder cancellation cannot catch anything
findings.body: The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...) } catch (error) { log.error(...) }` block wraps synchronous `forEach` calls over async functions. Since the returned promises are not awaited, any rejection from `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` escapes this catch as an unhandled rejection, and the log message is never produced. Await the calls (e.g. `await Promise.all(originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.map(...))`) so the error handling actually works and the cancellations complete before the reschedule continues.

findings.title: Cancellation window can be too late for SendGrid's cancellation deadline
findings.body: Cancellation is deferred to this CRON, which (per the PR description) runs every 15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. SendGrid only honours a cancel request if it arrives sufficiently ahead of the send time (documented as at least 10 minutes). If a booking is cancelled shortly after a CRON run and its reminder is due in ~15–25 minutes, the next run can reach SendGrid with less than 10 minutes to spare and the cancellation is rejected, so the reminder for the cancelled booking is still delivered. Consider cancelling immediately (or on a much tighter schedule) for reminders due within the next hour, or widening/short-circuiting the window.

findings.title: Type-only imports moved into a value import, and formatting will fail lint
findings.body: `PrismaPromise` is a type-only export of `@prisma/client` but is now pulled in through a value import, and the import list `  Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";` is missing the trailing comma required by the repo's prettier config, so `yarn lint`/format checks will fail on this file. Keep `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise } from "@prisma/client";` for the type-only names and run prettier (the large commented-out `testAction` block was also re-indented by this change, adding unrelated diff noise).
